questions.subtopic: Chapter 1: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants (Embryo Sac)
questions.question: A typical mature angiosperm female gametophyte (embryo sac) at the time of fertilization consists of what cellular and nuclear organization?

8-celled and 8-nucleate
7-celled and 7-nucleate
6-celled and 8-nucleate

questions.subtopic: Chapter 5: Molecular Basis of Inheritance (Hershey-Chase Experiment)
questions.question: In their 1952 bacteriophage experiment proving DNA as the genetic material, Hershey and Chase labeled DNA and protein coats respectively using which radioactive isotopes?

35S for DNA and 32P for protein coat
14C for DNA and 15N for protein coat
3H for DNA and 14C for protein coat
questions.explanation: DNA contains phosphorus but no sulfur, so it was labeled with 32P. Viral capsid proteins contain sulfur (in methionine and cysteine) but no phosphorus, so they were labeled with 35S. Only 32P entered the bacterial cells, proving DNA is the genetic material.

questions.subtopic: Chapter 6: Evolution (Hardy-Weinberg Principle)
questions.question: Which evolutionary factor disrupts the genetic equilibrium of a Mendelian population according to the Hardy-Weinberg law (p² + 2pq + q² = 1)?
options: Gene flow, genetic drift, mutation, genetic recombination, and natural selection
Random mating in an infinitely large population
Absence of differential reproductive mortality
Uniform environmental conditions over geological epochs
questions.explanation: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium holds when allele frequencies remain constant in the absence of evolutionary influences. Five factors disrupt this equilibrium: gene migration (gene flow), genetic drift, mutation, genetic recombination during meiosis, and natural selection.

questions.subtopic: Chapter 10: Biotechnology and Its Applications (Bt Cotton)
questions.question: Why does the crystalline Bt toxin produced by Bacillus thuringiensis kill lepidopteran insect larvae but not harm the host bacterium or mammalian digestive tracts?
options: The inactive protoxin is solubilized and activated only in the alkaline pH of the insect midgut, binding epithelial receptors to form lytic pores
Mammalian stomach acid activates the protoxin into a harmless vitamin
The bacterium contains antitoxin enzymes that hydrolyze all crystal proteins
The crystal protein binds only to plant cellulose microfibrils
questions.explanation: Bt toxin exists as an inactive crystal protoxin in bacteria. Ingested by insect larvae, the alkaline pH (>9.0) of the midgut solubilizes the crystals, and gut proteases cleave the protoxin into active toxin. The active toxin binds midgut epithelial receptors, creating pores that cause cell lysis and death.

questions.subtopic: Chapter 11: Organisms and Populations (Population Growth)
questions.question: In the logistic population growth equation dN/dt = rN[(K - N) / K], what does the term (K - N) / K represent ecologically?
options: Environmental resistance to population growth as carrying capacity K is approached
Intrinsic rate of natural increase under ideal un-limited conditions
Total mortality rate per thousand individuals
Net immigration rate across geographical borders
questions.explanation: In the Verhulst-Pearl logistic equation, (K - N) / K represents environmental resistance (fraction of carrying capacity still available). When N is small, this term is close to 1 (exponential growth); as N approaches K, (K - N) / K approaches 0, slowing growth to an asymptote.

questions.subtopic: Chapter 12: Biodiversity and Conservation (Species-Area Relationship)
questions.question: Alexander von Humboldt observed that within a region, species richness increases with explored area up to a limit. On a logarithmic scale, what is the mathematical equation of this relationship?
options: log S = log C + Z * log A
log S = log C - Z * log A
log S = Z * log C + log A
S = C * A^Z
questions.explanation: The species-area relationship is described by S = C * A^Z, where S is species richness, A is area, C is y-intercept, and Z is the slope of the regression line. On a log-log scale, it yields a straight line: log S = log C + Z * log A (where Z typically ranges between 0.1 and 0.2 for local areas).

questions.subtopic: Chapter 1: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants (Pollen & Tapetum)
questions.question: What is the primary function of the innermost anther wall layer, the tapetum, and what makes pollen exine remarkably resistant to degradation?
options: Tapetum nourishes developing pollen grains; pollen exine contains sporopollenin, one of the most resistant organic materials known
Tapetum performs mechanical dehiscence; exine contains cellulose and pectin without any polymers
Tapetum stores starch grains; exine contains calcium pectate that dissolves in dilute acids
Tapetum secretes sticky nectar; exine is composed of living protoplasmic proteins
questions.explanation: The anther wall consists of 4 layers: epidermis, endothecium, middle layers, and tapetum. The innermost layer, the tapetum, nourishes the developing pollen grains and its cells possess dense cytoplasm and generally more than one nucleus. The hard outer layer of pollen, the exine, is composed of sporopollenin, which withstands high temperatures, strong acids, and alkali, and no enzyme that degrades sporopollenin is known.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 1: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, Section 1.2.1 Stamen, Microsporangium and Pollen Grain

questions.subtopic: Chapter 1: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants (Cleistogamous Flowers)
questions.question: Plants like Viola (common pansy), Oxalis, and Commelina produce cleistogamous flowers. What is the key reproductive characteristic of these flowers?
options: They never open at all; anthers and stigma lie close, ensuring 100% autogamous pollination without requiring pollinating agents
They expose their anthers and stigma widely to the wind for anemophilous cross-pollination
They produce sweet nectar and large colourful petals exclusively adapted for entomophily
They are strictly unisexual female flowers that undergo obligatory xenogamy
questions.explanation: Cleistogamous flowers do not open at all. In such flowers, the anthers and stigma lie close to each other. When anthers dehisce in the flower buds, pollen grains come into contact with the stigma to effect pollination. Thus, cleistogamous flowers are invariably autogamous as there is no chance of cross-pollen landing on the stigma, ensuring an assured seed set even in the absence of pollinators.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 1: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, Section 1.2.3 Pollination

questions.subtopic: Chapter 2: Human Reproduction (Oogenesis Arrest Stages)
questions.question: At which specific stage of cell division are primary oocytes arrested in the human female ovary from embryonic life until puberty?
options: Metaphase-II of Meiosis II
Prophase-I (Diplotene stage) of Meiosis I
Anaphase-I of Meiosis I
Telophase-II of Meiosis II
questions.explanation: Oogenesis is initiated during the embryonic development stage when a couple of million gamete mother cells (oogonia) are formed within each foetal ovary. These cells start division and enter into Prophase-I of meiotic division and get temporarily arrested at that stage (diplotene), called primary oocytes, until puberty.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 2: Human Reproduction, Section 2.2 Gametogenesis

questions.subtopic: Chapter 3: Reproductive Health (IUD Types)
questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs an Intrauterine Device (IUD) category with its commercial clinical examples?
options: Non-medicated IUD — Lippes loop; Hormone-releasing IUD — Progestasert and LNG-20
Copper-releasing IUD — LNG-20 and Saheli; Non-medicated IUD — Multiload 375
Hormone-releasing IUD — CuT and Cu7; Copper-releasing IUD — Lippes loop
Barrier IUD — Vaults and Diaphragms; Chemical IUD — Spermicidal jellies
questions.explanation: Intrauterine Devices (IUDs) are classified into: (1) Non-medicated IUDs (e.g., Lippes loop); (2) Copper-releasing IUDs (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375); and (3) Hormone-releasing IUDs (Progestasert, LNG-20). Hormone-releasing IUDs make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperm.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 3: Reproductive Health, Section 3.2 Population Stabilization and Birth Control

questions.subtopic: Chapter 4: Principles of Inheritance (Pleiotropy in PKU)
questions.question: Phenylketonuria (PKU) in humans is a prime example of pleiotropy. What is the fundamental mechanism of this genetic disorder?
options: Mutation in a single gene encoding phenylalanine hydroxylase affects multiple phenotypic traits (mental retardation, skin depigmentation, and hair loss)
Non-disjunction of chromosome 21 leading to generalized intellectual and physical developmental delays
X-linked recessive mutation in blood clotting factor VIII leading to continuous haemorrhage
Trisomy of sex chromosomes (47, XXY) causing hypogonadism and sterile gynecomastia
questions.explanation: Pleiotropy occurs when a single gene can exhibit multiple phenotypic expressions. Phenylketonuria (PKU) is caused by mutation in the gene that codes for the enzyme phenylalanine hydroxylase. This single gene mutation results in mental retardation and reduction in hair and skin pigmentation due to systemic accumulation of phenylalanine and phenylpyruvic acid.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 4: Principles of Inheritance and Variation, Section 4.2.2.3 Pleiotropy

questions.subtopic: Chapter 4: Principles of Inheritance (Morgan's Drosophila Linkage)
questions.question: In his dihybrid crosses with Drosophila melanogaster, why did Thomas Hunt Morgan observe significant deviation from Mendel's 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 dihybrid ratio for eye colour and body colour genes?
options: The two genes are located on the same X-chromosome and are physically linked, suppressing independent assortment
The genes are situated on separate autosomes and undergo random non-homologous recombination
Eye colour is determined by multiple alleles showing co-dominance in female fruit flies
Female Drosophila undergo complete crossing-over suppression during gametogenesis
questions.explanation: T.H. Morgan crossed yellow-bodied, white-eyed females with brown-bodied, red-eyed males and found that the F2 ratio deviated significantly from 9:3:3:1. Morgan attributed this to physical linkage: when two genes in a dihybrid cross are situated on the same chromosome, the proportion of parental gene combinations is much higher than the non-parental (recombinant) type.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 4: Principles of Inheritance and Variation, Section 4.3 Linkage and Recombination

questions.subtopic: Chapter 5: Molecular Basis of Inheritance (Griffith Transforming Principle)
questions.question: In Frederick Griffith's 1928 transformation experiment with Streptococcus pneumoniae, what was the crucial experimental observation that proved bacterial transformation?
options: Mice injected with heat-killed virulent S-strain died of pneumonia within 24 hours
Mice injected with a mixture of heat-killed S-strain and living avirulent R-strain died of pneumonia, and living virulent S-strain was recovered
Mice injected with living R-strain developed severe bacteremia and internal haemorrhage
Protease enzyme treatment completely destroyed the transforming substance in pneumococcal lysates
questions.explanation: Griffith injected mice with a mixture of heat-killed virulent S-strain bacteria and living non-virulent R-strain bacteria. The mice died of pneumonia, and living virulent S-strain bacteria were recovered from their heart blood. Griffith concluded that the R-strain had somehow been transformed by the heat-killed S-strain into virulent smooth bacteria by a 'transforming principle'.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 5: Molecular Basis of Inheritance, Section 5.2.1 The Genetic Material is DNA

questions.subtopic: Chapter 5: Molecular Basis of Inheritance (Avery, MacLeod, McCarty Experiment)
questions.question: How did Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod, and Maclyn McCarty (1944) conclusively demonstrate that the transforming principle was DNA and not protein or RNA?
options: Digestion with proteases and RNases did not affect transformation, whereas digestion with DNase completely inhibited transformation
Treatment with sulfur-35 labeled bacteriophage capsids selectively destroyed viral protein coats
Gel filtration showed that pneumococcal capsular polysaccharide alone mediated transformation
Electron microscopy revealed the double-helical structure of transforming chromatin threads
questions.explanation: Avery, MacLeod, and McCarty purified biochemicals (proteins, DNA, RNA) from heat-killed S cells. They discovered that proteases (protein-digesting enzymes) and RNases (RNA-digesting enzymes) did not affect transformation. Only digestion with DNase (deoxyribonuclease) inhibited transformation, proving that DNA caused the transformation and is the chemical substance of heredity.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 5: Molecular Basis of Inheritance, Section 5.2.1 The Genetic Material is DNA

questions.subtopic: Chapter 6: Evolution (Adaptive Radiation of Darwin's Finches)
questions.question: The evolution of diverse beak shapes in Darwin's finches on the isolated Galapagos Islands from an original ancestral seed-eating finch is a classic example of:
options: Adaptive radiation resulting from divergent evolution in geographical isolation
Convergent evolution driven by identical ecological niches on the South American mainland
Industrial melanism caused by atmospheric pollution selecting for darker phenotypic morphs
Stabilizing natural selection eliminating peripheral phenotypic variants
questions.explanation: During his voyage on HMS Beagle, Darwin observed in Galapagos Islands an amazing diversity of finches on the same island group. All varieties evolved on the island itself from an original seed-eating stock into vegetarian and insectivorous forms with altered beaks. This process of evolution of different species in a given geographical area radiating to other habitats is called adaptive radiation (divergent evolution).
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 6: Evolution, Section 6.5 What is Adaptive Radiation?

questions.subtopic: Chapter 7: Human Health and Disease (Cancer Cell Properties)
questions.question: What is the cellular and physiological hallmark of malignant cancerous cells that distinguishes them from normal mammalian body cells?
options: Loss of contact inhibition and the dangerous property of metastasis (spreading to distant organs)
Strict limitation to a finite number of mitotic cell divisions in cell culture
Hyper-sensitivity to contact with adjacent cells leading to immediate apoptosis
Failure to synthesize cellular oncogenes or telomerase enzymes
questions.explanation: Normal cells show a property called contact inhibition by virtue of which contact with other cells inhibits their uncontrolled growth. Cancer cells lose contact inhibition, continuing to divide into tumors. Cells sloughed from malignant tumors reach distant sites through blood and start a new tumor wherever they lodge; this property, called metastasis, is the most feared characteristic of malignant cancers.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 7: Human Health and Disease, Section 7.5 Cancer

questions.subtopic: Chapter 8: Microbes in Human Welfare (Biocontrol Agents)
questions.question: Baculoviruses belonging to the genus Nucleopolyhedrovirus are celebrated in Integrated Pest Management (IPM) programs because they:
options: Are narrow-spectrum, species-specific insecticidal pathogens with no negative impacts on non-target plants, mammals, or birds
Are broad-spectrum chemical fumigants that eliminate all insects and soil nematodes universally
Produce non-biodegradable synthetic organophosphates that persist in agro-ecosystems for decades
Form mutualistic symbiotic nodules in the root cortex of leguminous crops
questions.explanation: Baculoviruses are pathogens that attack insects and other arthropods. The majority of baculoviruses used as biological control agents belong to the genus Nucleopolyhedrovirus. These viruses are excellent candidates for species-specific, narrow spectrum insecticidal applications and have been shown to have no negative impacts on plants, mammals, birds, fish or non-target insects.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 8: Microbes in Human Welfare, Section 8.3 Microbes as Biocontrol Agents

questions.subtopic: Chapter 8: Microbes in Human Welfare (Biofertilizers)
questions.question: Which cyanobacterium fixes atmospheric nitrogen and acts as an important biofertilizer in waterlogged paddy (rice) agricultural fields?
options: Anabaena and Nostoc
Lactobacillus acidophilus
Methanobacterium
Penicillium notatum
questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria are autotrophic microbes widely distributed in aquatic and terrestrial environments, many of which can fix atmospheric nitrogen: Anabaena, Nostoc, Oscillatoria, etc. In paddy fields, cyanobacteria serve as an indispensable biofertilizer while adding organic matter to the soil and increasing its fertility.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 8: Microbes in Human Welfare, Section 8.4 Microbes as Biofertilisers

questions.subtopic: Chapter 9: Biotechnology: Principles (Gene Gun vs Micro-injection)
questions.question: In recombinant transformation, which physical methods are typically deployed to introduce recombinant DNA into plant cells and animal cells respectively?
options: Biolistics (Gene gun) coated with gold/tungsten micro-particles for plants, and Micro-injection directly into nucleus for animals
Electroporation with lysozyme for plants, and Heat-shock calcium chloride treatment for animals
Micro-injection into vacuoles for plants, and Biolistics particle bombardment for animals
Ultrasonication for plants, and Disarmed retroviral immersion for animals
questions.explanation: For animal cells, recombinant DNA is directly micro-injected into the nucleus of an animal egg or embryo using a fine micropipette. In plant cells, cells are bombarded with high-velocity micro-particles of gold or tungsten coated with foreign DNA in a method known as biolistics or gene gun.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 9: Biotechnology: Principles and Processes, Section 9.2.3 Competent Host (For Transformation with Recombinant DNA)

questions.subtopic: Chapter 9: Biotechnology: Principles (Stirred-Tank Bioreactors)
questions.question: What is the primary advantage of a sparged stirred-tank bioreactor over a simple stirred-tank bioreactor in large-scale microbial culture?
options: Sterile air bubbles are sparged through the reactor, dramatically increasing the surface area for oxygen transfer
It eliminates the necessity for temperature and pH sensory control systems
It operates entirely without mechanical impellers or foam-control agitators
It produces non-recombinant secondary metabolites without requiring sterilization
questions.explanation: A stirred-tank reactor is usually cylindrical with a curved base to facilitate mixing. In a sparged stirred-tank bioreactor, sterile air is sparged (bubbled) through the culture medium. The bubbles dramatically increase the surface area for gas-liquid mass transfer, ensuring high dissolved oxygen availability throughout the large culture volume (100–1000 litres).
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 9: Biotechnology: Principles and Processes, Section 9.3 Bioreactors

questions.subtopic: Chapter 10: Biotechnology and its Applications (Transgenic Cow Rosie)
questions.question: In 1997, the first transgenic cow, named 'Rosie', produced human-protein enriched milk. Which human protein was synthesized in her milk, making it nutritionally superior for infants?
options: Human alpha-lactalbumin (2.4 grams per litre)
Human insulin (Eli Lilly chain A and B)
Human alpha-1-antitrypsin for emphysema
Human tissue plasminogen activator (tPA)
questions.explanation: In 1997, the first transgenic cow, Rosie, produced human protein-enriched milk (2.4 grams per litre). The milk contained the human gene for alpha-lactalbumin and was nutritionally more balanced for human babies than natural cow-milk.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 10: Biotechnology and its Applications, Section 10.3 Transgenic Animals

questions.subtopic: Chapter 10: Biotechnology and its Applications (Gene Therapy for ADA Deficiency)
questions.question: In 1990, the first clinical gene therapy was given to a 4-year-old girl suffering from Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency causing severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID). What was the therapeutic procedure?
options: Lymphocytes extracted from the patient's blood were cultured, transformed with functional ADA cDNA using a retroviral vector, and re-infused into the patient
Bone marrow cells were permanently replaced with genetically engineered porcine embryonic stem cells
Synthetic ADA protein was administered once orally in enterically coated liposomes
A functional ADA gene was injected directly into fertilized zygotes using nuclear transfer
questions.explanation: The first clinical gene therapy was given in 1990 to a 4-year-old girl with adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency. Lymphocytes from the blood of the patient were grown in culture outside the body. A functional ADA cDNA (using a retroviral vector) was introduced into these lymphocytes, which were subsequently returned to the patient. Because these cells are not immortal, the patient requires periodic infusion of genetically engineered lymphocytes.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 10: Biotechnology and its Applications, Section 10.2.2 Gene Therapy

questions.subtopic: Chapter 11: Organisms and Populations (Gause's Competitive Exclusion Principle)
questions.question: According to Gause's Competitive Exclusion Principle:
options: Two closely related species competing for the exact same limiting resources cannot co-exist indefinitely, and the competitively inferior one will eventually be eliminated
Two species competing for resources will always evolve resource partitioning to achieve stable co-existence
Predators always overexploit their prey populations, causing mutual extinction within isolated ecosystems
Herbivore populations are limited exclusively by carnivore predation rather than plant biomass availability
questions.explanation: Gause's 'Competitive Exclusion Principle' states that two closely related species competing for the same limiting resources cannot co-exist indefinitely and the competitively inferior one will be eliminated eventually. While resource partitioning (as shown by MacArthur's warblers) can allow coexistence, the classic principle describes exclusion under strict non-partitioned resource limitation.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 11: Organisms and Populations, Section 11.2 Population Interactions

questions.subtopic: Chapter 12: Ecosystem (Decomposition Steps)
questions.question: What is the correct chronological sequence of biological and physical processes involved in the decomposition of detritus in an ecosystem?
options: Fragmentation -> Leaching -> Catabolism -> Humification and Mineralization
Mineralization -> Catabolism -> Leaching -> Fragmentation -> Humification
Humification -> Fragmentation -> Mineralization -> Catabolism -> Leaching
Leaching -> Mineralization -> Humification -> Fragmentation -> Catabolism
questions.explanation: The important steps in the process of decomposition are: (1) Fragmentation (earthworms break detritus into smaller particles); (2) Leaching (water-soluble inorganic nutrients seep into soil horizon and precipitate); (3) Catabolism (bacterial and fungal enzymes degrade detritus into simpler inorganic substances); followed by (4) Humification (leads to accumulation of dark amorphous humus) and (5) Mineralization (release of inorganic nutrients).
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 12: Ecosystem, Section 12.2 Decomposition

questions.subtopic: Chapter 13: Biodiversity and Conservation (Rivet Popper Hypothesis)
questions.question: In the Rivet Popper hypothesis proposed by Stanford ecologist Paul Ehrlich to explain the importance of species diversity in an ecosystem:
options: The airplane represents the ecosystem, rivets represent individual species, and popping rivets on wings represents the extinction of key foundation species that imperils system safety
The airplane represents atmospheric ozone, rivets represent CFC molecules, and wings represent thermal solar radiation
The airplane represents agricultural monoculture, rivets represent pesticide formulations, and wings represent crop yield
The airplane represents industrial technology, rivets represent genetic engineers, and wings represent commercial biopesticides
questions.explanation: Paul Ehrlich used an analogy: In an airplane (ecosystem) with thousands of rivets (species), if passengers start popping rivets to take home, it may not disrupt flight safety initially. But as more rivets are removed, the plane becomes dangerously weak over time. Furthermore, popping rivets on the wings (key species that drive major ecosystem functions) poses a much more immediate threat to flight safety than removing rivets on seats inside.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 13: Biodiversity and Conservation, Section 13.1.3 The Importance of Species Diversity to the Ecosystem

questions.subtopic: Chapter 13: Biodiversity and Conservation (Evil Quartet of Biodiversity Loss)
questions.question: According to ecologists, what is the most important cause driving animals and plants to extinction among 'The Evil Quartet'?
options: Habitat loss and fragmentation (e.g., clearing of the Amazon rainforest for soybean cultivation)
Over-exploitation for commercial trade (e.g., Steller's sea cow and passenger pigeon)
Alien species invasions (e.g., Nile perch in Lake Victoria and Parthenium weed)
Co-extinctions in obligate mutualisms (e.g., specialized plant-pollinator mutualisms)
questions.explanation: Habitat loss and fragmentation is the most important cause driving animal and plant species to extinction. The most dramatic examples of habitat loss come from tropical rainforests: once covering more than 14% of the earth's land surface, these now cover no more than 6%. The Amazon rainforest ('lungs of the planet') is being cut and cleared for cultivating soya beans or for conversion to grasslands for beef cattle.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 13: Biodiversity and Conservation, Section 13.1.4 Loss of Biodiversity
